description: How the municipal enforcement roles relate to each other: who mandates and funds the program, who hands incidents to whom, how fine revenue returns to the budget, and which reporting loops prove visible results to residents.

relationTypes.name: Commercial
relationTypes.description: Mandating, funding, and commissioning of enforcement and cleanliness services

relationTypes.name: Operational
relationTypes.description: Day-to-day incident handoff, dispatch, and field coordination

relationTypes.name: Financial
relationTypes.description: Fine revenue, cleanup cost recovery, and budget settlement

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Hotspot intelligence, compliance posture, and performance reporting

relations.name: Mandates and funds the enforcement program
relations.description: Sponsors the camera-based enforcement pilot, sets neighborhood priorities, and allocates the budget and legal mandate under which local police operate the program.

relations.name: Sets cleanliness service levels and budget
relations.description: Commissions cleanliness operations with explicit service levels for cleanup response times and funds the crews and equipment needed to keep hotspots visibly clean.

relations.name: Hands off secured incidents for cleanup
relations.description: Releases dumping sites for removal once evidence is secured and the case file is complete, so cleanup crews can be dispatched without compromising enforceability.

relations.name: Flags recurring dumping hotspots
relations.description: Reports recurring dump locations, waste types, and field observations from cleanup rounds so enforcement can target cameras and patrols where offenses actually cluster.

relations.name: Reports enforcement outcomes and compliance posture
relations.description: Delivers case, identification, and sanction statistics together with the GDPR compliance posture of the program, giving the mayor defensible numbers for council and press.

relations.name: Proves cleanliness performance
relations.description: Reports cleanup response times, recurrence rates, and cost per incident so the mayor can show residents visible improvement per neighborhood.

relations.name: Returns fine revenue to the municipal budget
relations.description: Feeds fines collected from enforceable dumping cases back into the municipal budget, offsetting part of the enforcement and cleanup cost the mayor must justify.
